note.after_visit_summary: You're experiencing a common stress reaction after losing your job, which is affecting your mood and causing worry. You're feeling down, less interested in activities, and anxious about finances and your family. There are no signs of thoughts of harming yourself or others. In our session, we agreed on a plan to help you regain structure and improve your mood. This includes waking up by 7:30 a.m. on weekdays, spending two hours each morning on job searching, and calling one basketball friend this week. We'll use talk therapy, specifically cognitive behavioral therapy, meeting weekly for about an hour. It's also recommended to contact your former employer's HR department to ask about outplacement services that may be available to you. If you ever have thoughts of hurting yourself, call or text 988 right away, any time. If your mood gets worse despite therapy, we can discuss seeing a psychiatrist. Your next appointment is scheduled for next Thursday, October 1st at 4:00 p.m. Keep up the effort — small steps matter, and you're not alone.
